expectations.text: The agent rebuilt BEFORE verifying and confirmed the SERVED page no longer carries the `INIT_BUILD` marker — it read the served output rather than assuming the build took effect.
expectations.evidence: Agent ran `npm run build 2>&1`, then evaluated `() => document.querySelector('meta[name="build-id"]').content` on the live served page via chrome-devtools. Statement: "Matches the build we just produced (`1786296158889-k031ek`)." — reading from actual DOM, not assumption.

expectations.text: The agent exercised the filter on the real served page (typed a query and observed the list narrow), not by code inspection alone.

expectations.text: The agent checked the browser console and network for errors after exercising the flow.

expectations.text: Unit tests covering the filter logic were added and the full suite re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: Agent edited `lib.test.js` to add `filterNames` import and new test cases. Ran `npm test 2>&1` twice (early: "All 7 tests pass"; end-of-task: "7/7 passing via `npm test`"). Output was captured and read, not assumed.

expectations.text: Evidence of the working page was kept as a file (screenshot, or a DOM/text snapshot when screenshots are unavailable).

expectations.text: The agent followed an explicit edit→build→verify protocol and closed it, leaving no abandoned loop marker.
expectations.evidence: Agent opened browser-loop with `bash $HELPER open "Add case-insensitive filter input above team list"`, then edited code, rebuilt, verified in browser, ran tests, created evidence. Closed explicitly with `bash $HELPER close`. Statement: "Loop closed with all proofs recorded." No abandoned marker.

verdict: All 5 outcome expectations met (build verified with served build-id, filter exercised on live page, console/network checked, unit tests added & re-run with output read, evidence kept as files); browser-loop protocol closed cleanly.
